reviews.title: Exponential Idle - A mindless idle game like the others
reviews.text:
This game at first appears to be just a smarter, but more simple design. No cookies to click. Just a mathematical equation. As you continuously progress in the game you get to experience the complex equations that start to happen. Adding more variables using “Stars” which unlike most idle games is able to get while having fun. 

Just as I started thinking wow, this game really isn’t that fun. I got to the prestige part, I had clicked the first equation about 8,000 times. I reached a point where my f(t) wasn’t going up that much anymore and then I became able to prestige. This changed everything I was then getting higher and higher until I reached around ee100 then I got introduced to Supremacy. Eventually getting auto buyers, then an auto prestiger. I could then AFK for around 4-8 hours come back and supremacy. I am currently sitting at ee730 and waiting to get the achievement for reachi

reviews.title: Not impressed. Ironically simple
reviews.text:
So far I’ve gone through 2 iterations of “prestige” and reached the fourth variable. Compared to other idle games, the growth equation of Exponential Idle seems too basic, which makes the game kinda boring for me. It’s kinda ironic that the equation is so simple, given that the theme of the game is exponential math. Maybe it gets more complex later? But I have little interest in playing to get to that point.

To explain what I mean - in the game you build up your independent variable X (thereby improving your f(x) function), and you also level up other sub-variables to do it. The function is just X = 0.8*Xlv + 2*(Ylv+Zlv+Slv). Basically the contribution of Y, Z, and S (per level) are exactly the same, so you end just level up whichever one is cheaper... kinda boring. Also the contribution of leveling X is just 40% as much as leveling the others, and it’s free to do so but you can only gi

reviews.title: Don’t let the complexity scare you away
reviews.text:
I really enjoyed this game. You can enjoy it on a couple different (intellectual) levels. First, it’s just a very fun idle game that is quite well balanced. Upgrades come and take a bit of time and then the things that become bothersome to manage become automatic. 

Second, it’s a game about math. For most of the equations you don’t need to understand them to progress. At the very end of the game there are some that you will need to understand, but that’s a very small part of the game and some web searching or a helpful soul on discord will get you sorted out.   I’m an electrical engineer and thought the equations were well thought out and straightforward, although there was one that still confuses me to this day, but that wasn’t one I needed to know. 

There is no pay wall, just watch and ad to get a few hours of boosted progress. Or pay a small one time transaction to always be boosted

reviews.title: A simple and interesting game
reviews.text:
This is a really simple game. Basically it allows players to modify the parameters of a function, and the goal is to push the function value as high as possible (and as fast as possible). 
What’s interesting about the game is that the player does not need to understand the actual formula. The player can test different parameters to get a feeling of rate of the change; and slowly moving toward the “optimal” parameter.

I rated this game 4 stars because I believe there are many other ways to improve the game. 

Imagining if we could map the function to another space, which would reflect the overall growth of the original function. It could brings a more intuitive way for players to evaluate the growth of the function by changing certain variables. 

Or map the function to a random space, in which it would draw something chaotic. Every time the player opens the game up, he/she could see a f

reviews.title: My life after exponential idle
reviews.text:
Exponential idle is not a game, it’s a lifestyle and a culture. My life has completely changed after downloading this game. I have lost everything I had except for this game. I was fired from my job for exponential idling too competitively. I now live in a homeless shelter and survive off of social security checks. I need food stamps to survive now, I have lost everything from this game. My wife divorced me, and took the kids. Bertha was originally supportive of my idling lifestyle. But then as the debt grew, she became more discriminatory about my idling culture. I decided that she was the issue and needed to be erased from my life. I have given you everything, and in return I have achieved eternal happiness knowing that I am the greatest idler to ever exist.

-Brian Zang Sub

reviews.title: I bet it’s a great game
reviews.text: I don’t really understand it. I’m taking calculus 2 and I still trying to wrap my head around the various methods of integration and series/sums of convergence and divergence. Im not doing well in the class tbh. I just keep pressing random variables. Is the goal to have the function runaway exponentially? Like x^x? Or something reaching infinity near a vertical asymptote? It keeps leveling out in rocket fashion like a square root function. That’s annoying lol but I still like to see the graph change as I press variables. Too many variables though. I don’t even see all of them, but maybe it’s just because I don’t understand. Or maybe I have to figure out what those variables do? Even though they’re not explicitly written in the function? People are saying it’s a fun game nonetheless

reviews.title: Surprisingly good!
reviews.text:
When I first downloaded this game, I was bit expecting much. Just another idle game (which I am admittedly a fan of) that I might drop after a few weeks. However, I was surprised at the depth of this game and how well the gameplay integrates into the story. I especially enjoy the theories, though I do wish they would be better explained. For example, I don’t fully understand “Numerical Methods” and a short explanation of what each variable means would benefit me a lot instead of jumping right in into the symbols and notation.

Overall, though, a very good game. There are some slow parts and some guesswork involved, but I enjoy the grind.

reviews.title: Great game!
reviews.text: Obviously there is waiting involved (it’s in the name of the game) but after a bit there is a good bit to do and solve. No necessary in game purchases nor ads. Even when you leave the game it continues without you and after a bit you can automate things making leaving easier. I pick up the game for maybe 5 minutes every few hours and the point where I am in the game. I am very satisfied with how simplistic this game is on the surface but I know there was some serious math involved in the creation of this and I give props to the creators for there hard work. 10/10 game amazing!

reviews.title: If only there were more games like this
reviews.text:
This is exactly what I wanted when mobile games began to take over the market. It’s simple, fun, there’s zero pressure to pay for anything, and there’s a finish. 

What I appreciate the most is there is an end to this incremental game. It takes a while to get to obviously and the creator is always adding new features but there’s a end point you want to reach. 

This alone solves so many problems with how mobile games are today with the pay to win model and the GACHA character collection part of most idle games these days. They never want to lose you as a customer so they never put a finish to the game. This feels like you’re progressing through a story which has a goal. No loot boxes or extra currencies. 

This is the perfect idle game. It is what every idle game should strive to be and I really hope that people take notice of how you can be successful without throwing a billion ads in e

reviews.title: The best idle game I’ve ever played
reviews.text:
This game is the most mechanically deep idle game I’ve ever played. Custom automation gets rid of the most monotonous parts of this genre while challenging you to think mathematically. Multiple levels of prestige and the unique mini games help keep the game interesting. 

The pacing is almost perfect. Progress normally happens fairly quickly and, when it doesn’t, using a good automation expressions lets you sit back and wait for the speed to catch up again.

I have no complaints outside of occasional lag on the mini games, which can be annoying if you’re trying to beat your top time.

reviews.title: Incredibly entertaining
reviews.text: Typical idle games are soulless and mindless games that have no substance. This one is far different. Every stage of the game is new and rewarding. Figuring out the mini game puzzles is gratifying. I did have to look up the arrow ones but even figuring out those algorithms was fun. As soon as a part of the game gets boring, the process gets automated. Fantastic free to play idle game not littered with micro transactions, with some soul put into it. Also, try to do secret achievement 13 without looking it up. You’ll feel like a detective

reviews.title: Good game, but progression after theories is insanely slow
reviews.text: After unlocking recurrence relations, my progress has just stagnated. I’ve tried using 100s of thousands of stars to try and upgrade variables and many different combinations of student upgrades, but at this point every prestige takes more than a day and it’s been a while since a supremacy. I’m positive that I can be doing something better but the game gives you very little instruction. Still, up to this point it’s been a nice game when I’m bored, and I appreciate how there are no ads unless you initiate them.

reviews.title: Great game, with some performance issues
reviews.text:
The game is really fun and the mechanical complexity is well thought out for an idle game. The various prestige systems have been interesting to discover and experiment with.
My largest complaint is that performance can be a bit spotty at times. Turning my graph quality to low seems to have helped, but even letting the game sit without doing anything sees dropped frames. Using the accelerator button, playing the mini games and immediately after prestiging the performance issues seem to worsen. Overall though the game is still playable and this is more an inconvenience than anything else.

reviews.title: Nothing but the math
reviews.text: Lots of other games have some sort of underlying math that paces out progression, giving a quick jolt of improvement, slowing down, and then jumping ahead to another layer of progression. What if we stripped away everything extra; no graphics aside from graphs and well rendered formulas, no characters outside of text, no controls, not even color! All that’s left is the math, ramped up to ridiculous extremes using notation I didn’t even know existed for absurdly huge numbers.

reviews.title: Beautiful concept beautifully executed
reviews.text:
Firstly, I’m just dipping my toes into math and found this game some time back. Having learned some calculus, I greatly appreciate the effort that went into this game so much more. Most clicker games are cut and paste but this one feels true. As if the internals to all of the others have been laid bare and exposed for my gaming. It’s paced very well and the progression is satisfying. Haven’t finished story mode but I’m enjoying it so far. 

If you’re thinking of getting it, I recommend it.

reviews.title: Sounds design
reviews.text: The actual gameplay? Totally awesome. The design of the UI? Love it. The sound design though? I can’t describe it. It’s heavenly. Even if you don’t like idle games, get the game JUST so you can experience the awesomeness that is the creamy clicky sounds when you tap stuff. Even if this was just an app with a button for the sound, I swear I would use it constantly while doing other stuff. It makes my brain melt. I wish I could give it six stars.

reviews.title: Shut up and take my money!
reviews.text:
Genuinely clever incremental game. The math looks intimidating but you don't actually need to understand it to play and progress — though it might make you curious enough to learn. Clean design, no predatory monetization, and it respects your time whether you play actively or let it idle.

My one complaint is that I'd happily give the developer more money than the current IAP options allow. If you ever add a bigger tip jar, I'm in.

reviews.title: Overall, a very solid take on the idle genre!
reviews.text:
This game has a very interesting concept and accompanying storyline to follow a traditional idle experience.
No involuntary ads and ads are not necessary to progress at a reasonable rate.

There are a few bugs including some "soft crashes" where the game will stop functioning but will not automatically close, but nothing that a quick restart wont fix :)

reviews.title: Play to the end!
reviews.text: This game has more surprises and respect for the user than I would have thought possible in any game, much less an idle game. You do not need to understand any formulas or even like math to get to the end of the game. If you do like math, it helps a little, but mostly you just understand better why you like the game so dang much. Try it! Click all the buttons and play to ee50

reviews.title: User Friendly
reviews.text:
This game lets the player actually dive deep into it without being bombarded by ads, given an impossible progression system requiring payment. I feel like I’m back in 2009, when mobile games were build with love and actually designed to entertain, not just make the developer money. 

This is easily in my top 3 mobile games list!

reviews.title: Great Game
reviews.text: While intimidating at first, getting into the game and automating the equation is some of the most fun I’ve had with an idle game. Add on the story line and multiple moving parts and this game is near perfect. The only complaint is that starting out is extremely difficult and tedious and I would prefer for the x= section to be able to have infinite exponents added like the y,z,c and all other equations.

reviews.title: Unique and Interesting
reviews.text: I haven’t seen an idle game with this style of progression yet, so that makes the game pretty interesting as a concept. Using an exponential formula as the points system makes a lot of sense, and it is implemented very well. I like the graph that shows your points over time, particularly how it smooths out when using the accelerate feature. I hope the developer continues to add more interesting features to the game.

reviews.title: Confusing
reviews.text:
I have no idea what’s going on. The formulas and numbers don’t make sense to me. I’m just pressing buttons with only a slight idea as to what they do, and then waiting here and there for the numbers to climb before progressing, only to start the process all over again from scratch.

That being said, this is my favorite idle app and I became addicted almost immediately. Amazing.

reviews.title: Amazing time killer
reviews.text: The game can be a bit intimidating and confusing at first especially if you aren’t savvy with math but it is one of those games the more you play the more you understand it. It doesn’t force ads whatsoever and the boost they apply never feels like it’s forced to progress past a certain point. The game is continuously updated and you can tell the developer cares about their product.

reviews.title: Hits the niche perfectly
reviews.text: Really engaging game, I feel that while the game is still easily playable without a deep understanding of all the mathematics involved it still rewards you for it being the case.  Very tight knit community built around the game and a very involved and honest developer.  Game is not going for your wallet.  Haven’t had this much fun on my phone in years, thank you so much!

reviews.title: Never get bored
reviews.text: Honestly, I never got bored of the game, although I’ve only had it for a month now, the story to it is really nice and it keeps the player entertained and to stay when maybe things are getting slow and you do have to start being idle for large amounts of time. I usually play a little bit, check back to see my progress and then sleep, rinse and repeat.

reviews.title: The game for me
reviews.text: I love idle games, have since I was a kid. I would play them over and over, prestige to the max, then delete the save entirely to truly start again. Maybe this is where I started to fall in love with numbers in a computer. I am now getting a PhD in applied mathematics and I find this idle game. It’s perfect. As they say in asymptotics, 4 is basically infinity, so 5/5 stars is \infty/5 stars.

reviews.title: Not forgiving at all
reviews.text: I have two young kids who frequently get ahold of my phone when I’m not paying attention. Turns out they ended up changing the date to 2 weeks in the future. When I set it back, the game said I could either be locked out for 2 weeks, or reset my game entirely. Devs could have just programmed the game to revert idle progress when a time change happened but instead the lazy devs have it set to ban you from the game. Looks like I can’t play since I have kids. Was a fun game while it lasted but I can’t promote a game with such an unnecessary and harsh function.

reviews.title: One of the best idle games
reviews.text: I’m a bit of a math nerd so this may be biased, but I really love the idea of exponential growth and being able to upgrade specific variables in the equation to increase growth. I also like how many “auto-clicker” options are available, including auto-prestige. The only thing I’d like is more minigames to play to get stars, because so far I’ve just been doing the easy 15-puzzle.

reviews.title: Best Idle Game Ever!
reviews.text: Exponential Idle is by far one of the best idle games I have ever played. I’m not going to go into detail because there are already multiple reviews which do so. If you just want something you can mess around with while on the metro or bus, maybe when you get home from school or when you first wake up, this is the game for you.

reviews.title: The most respectful idle game
reviews.text: You won’t find an idle game more respectful of the player. No forced ads after purchase, no ads whatsoever after purchase. No other purchases available besides removing ads. This game was not built to siphon money towards the dev, it was built to be fun (if you like this sort of thing)

reviews.title: Great, but one problem
reviews.text:
This is a very great game! There should be more games like this, but I just have one problem.

Whenever you collect your idle rewards, and go to 15 puzzle, the blocks start glitching out.

Even though that problem exists, I think this is the best game I have seen so far!

reviews.title: A small suggestion
reviews.text: I feel the way the db Graduation Research is handled should be changed because I did the math in Desmos and the highest nember it would let me try as an input resulted in an output of about 56 meanwhile I can just Research the Star one more and multiply everything by over 1.61 million and quickly rising. For reference, for every Research into Stars, I need to do FOUR Research into db, which is NOT economically viable.

reviews.title: The most user friendly game
reviews.text: I’ll keep it simple, stupid. In depth descriptions of every part of the game (with the addition of humor). Absolutely no forced ads. The game feels like it was made by a player not a developer (in a good way). Not a long, nor descriptive review but I feel it deserves something.

reviews.title: This game was made really well
reviews.text: There are no ads with or without Wi-Fi. That makes it the only mobile exclusive game with no forced ads. Also, this game has a real story and actually fun gameplay. You can’t get better than that. But wait! It also has good visuals! Strange notation/10

reviews.title: One of the best clickers out there
reviews.text: i NEVER leave reviews on games, but this one was just too good not to give 5 stars. I’m too lazy to write a paragraph on this, but you should definitely consider getting this game if you’re looking for a calming, quality idle with no ads or anything in your face

reviews.title: Phenomenal
reviews.text:

At the very least, it’s worth a download, you won’t disappointed, especially if you’re remotely interested in math.

reviews.title: Amazing Game
reviews.text: This game is a joy to play, and I am so sad that I finished the game. The concept of having a story to an idle game is unique, and I love the fact that its actually an idle game, theres no point to stay on the app for more than ten minutes to grind. Overall, my only qualm with this game is that its too short (or maybe i love it too much haha)

reviews.title: Bigger numbers on the App Store
reviews.text: Wow. I’m still early in my play through, but seeing a double exponent of 200+ is insane. There’s 200 digits in the number that describes the number of digits of the final value. Insanity. Vastly larger than any number that could be physically expressed in this universe. Love it

reviews.title: Best game ever

reviews.title: Simple yet sweet
reviews.text:
Do not be fooled by it's sophisticated appearance. It is an idle game that holds its special qualities such as a likable story. Its system is also not discombobulated once you get used to it. While there are only two mini-games, they require no RNG to obtain your reward(s). 
The game is one for those who like ease and simplicity.

reviews.title: Game just dies out
reviews.text:
After you supremecy for the first two upgrades, it takes 5 days to get the next.

I enjoyed the limited ads and it was fun, but there is just literally no point to opening the game. Theres nothing to be done but wait wait wait. Nothing to click to accelerate it.

Just wait wait wait. Literally just log in once a day and say "cool, guess I will log in in a couple more days to see if I can do anything.

reviews.title: Great game, at this point it plays itself!
reviews.text: This game is fun, but what i did allows the game to play itself which is ironically very fun because i can come back at any time and play it without stressing about lost time!

Even 2 straight weeks of automated prestige, buying, and supremacy, and I haven’t supremacy-ed. With no way to reinvest points in the students, I can only assume that I‘m screwed. 4 months of work only to hit a dead end in the game.

reviews.title: Awesome game
reviews.text: I can say that I was a bit skeptical when I first got it because it did look quite complex, but I’ve found out that it is very simple and is very fun! I would highly recommend it if you like a nice idle game.

reviews.title: A total nerd-gasm

Ya’ll hit it out of the park on this one.

If you like idle games try it.  If you like math try it.  If, like me, you fall into both of those camps then start enjoying now.

reviews.title: Honestly an amazing game

reviews.title: Simply fun

reviews.title: Pretty fun
reviews.text: This is a pretty interesting one. Been looking for an idle game that can keep going while offline, this one does it. There isn’t a lot to the graphics, but there doesn’t need to be. Simple, fun and engaging. The puzzles are also very intriguing.

reviews.title: Something to share

reviews.title: A Perfectly Wonderful ‘Game’ for the right kind of person
reviews.text:
For the right kind of person (complex, inquisitive, technical, and a little geeky, like I am, haha), this is a ‘game’ that will captivate and fascinate you. You don’t really need to know or perform any mathematical calculations or do any programming….don’t be intimidated by the formulas that are at the core of the game. They work by themselves, and you’ll never need a calculator or even a pencil and paper. BUT, I won’t lie, the more math and programming courses you once took, the more you will enjoy the game, remembering things from your distant past. 

Exponential idle starts out as a clicker game, but honestly, that doesn’t last very long. Maybe half an hour. Then, it becomes an ‘idle’ game, but that’s really a misnomer too, because you’ll never be idle in Exponential Idle.
